summary.intent: Confirm whether the npm publish-confirmation (observation) step needs the same private-registry credentials as the publish itself, and fix it if not.
summary.outcome: Confirmed the bug: the release action gives NPM_TOKEN to the publish child only as a temporary npm config, so `npm view` ran anonymously and got 404 on restricted packages. Fixed by passing the same config via --userconfig, added a test and changeset, committed and pushed on fix/npm-observation-credentials, then attempted to link a trail and look up a PR number (result not shown).

repo: The release action converts NPM_TOKEN into a temporary npm config handed only to the publish child process, so the observation child never saw it.
Tokens in the environment and project or user .npmrc already reached both publish and observation children equally; only the temp config was missed.
Anonymous `npm view` on a restricted package returns 404, so the confirmation polls through its whole window and fails with E157; reruns fail the same way.

Subprocess runners and env-filtering helpers live in crates/callisto-cli/src/runner.rs; registry observation code is in crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/registry/ (npm.rs, cargo.rs, tests.rs).
Callisto's own release publishes only to crates.io and GitHub and has no NPM_TOKEN, so it is not affected by this bug.
Changes use .changeset/*.md files, and checks run with cargo fmt, cargo test --offline -p callisto-graph --lib, and cargo clippy -D warnings.

code.finding: npm observation runs `npm view`; it was changed to pass the publisher's npm config via --userconfig when one is set.
The release script builds the temporary npm config from NPM_TOKEN for the publish step.

workflow: Verify an earlier review finding against the code before acting on it.
Branch from a freshly fetched origin/main for an unrelated fix instead of committing on the existing worktree branch.
Use `--offline` for cargo test and clippy runs to avoid network access.

friction: The user was frustrated that the observation step lacked credentials the publish step had.
The final command chain used `tail -1` on the push and trail-link output, so the outcomes of the push, trail link, and PR lookup were not visible.
open_items: No PR was confirmed as created; the PR number lookup result is unknown and the branch may still need a PR.
The trail link to entire for 198 was attempted but its result is not shown.
